coverage.assessment: The chain from approach to request, warning, instructions, hand-off and boat is intact. The meaning of a silent ad (he is dead) was lost in the first draft, which slightly weakens the setup for Danvers's fate.
Time, ship, lineup, first-class stranger and the palm-to-palm transfer are all clear. Both characters remain unnamed. The compressed list sentence still sends her to the boat.
Turn-taking is clean, but the girl no longer answers 'Have you the nerve' directly. She answers only 'real proud to be chosen', so the reply is a non sequitur.
'I don't think I have, but one never knows' is preserved verbatim. So are 'may make all the difference' and 'not more than eighteen'.
The narration stays close to the girl's perception. Nothing about Danvers, Jane or the followers is disclosed early.
The grave, short-exchange register holds. Minor trims flatten the man's self-sacrificing logic and the staged loud farewell; these are tradeoffs.
The contrast between his fear and her steadiness is retained, as is the 'women and children first' logic.
Dependencies 0 and 1 are intact at both ends. Dependency 2 is intact locally, but chapter 026's revision cut the 'shadowed from New York … didn't think so' echo.

strengths: All four verbatim lines are preserved exactly, including the muttered 'It must be!… it is the only way.'
The paradox that his fear is not fear of death is kept with its exclamatory narratorial close.
The girl's idiom ('I guess…', 'real proud') and her grave, steadfast characterization are retained.
The quiet-climax rhythm of the hand-off line, given its own paragraph, is intact.
summary: The revision is a faithful, compact prologue. Every essential beat, all four verbatim lines, both anonymities, the 'Shipmate'/Times/three-days/Ambassador instructions and the girl's American idiom survive. The losses are small. The revision cut the girl's direct answer to the 'nerve' question and the 'personal column' detail. The first draft had already dropped 'down and out', which gave the three-day silence its meaning, and the 'be ready' cue that frames the loud good-bye as cover. Dependencies 0 and 1 are intact. Dependency 2 survives locally, but its partner in chapter 026 lost the echoing 'shadowed … didn't think so' line.
